criterion.purpose: one pre-registered intervention on top of round23: change the privileged auxiliary label from "the gap is on which side of the playfield centre" to "the gap is on which side OF THE PLAYER", i.e. from a position fact to the action sign that closes the distance, and read the result out with a judgement rule that can say "worse"

intervention.change: the auxiliary label only: sign(gap screen centre - player screen x) instead of gap screen centre > 192; the head, its placement, the loss, the weight, the arms, the seeds, the updates, the data and the split are round23's
intervention.task: from the GRU state predict whether the safe gap lies left or right OF THE PLAYER, i.e. which sign of action closes the distance to the slot: label = sign(gap screen centre - player screen x), gap from round21.telegraph_gap(s) (privileged world parameter), player x from the frozen teacher trajectory (train) or the checkpoint's own trajectory (scoring); the label is read at the first row of the telegraph window

label.source: `round21.telegraph_gap(s)` for the gap (the privileged world parameter, exactly the arithmetic the R21 renderer draws the band with) and the player screen x, which `render_state` draws at 32+state.x and `advance` moves by 2*action: so the label is the sign of the action that reduces the distance to the slot
label.reference: the player x, not the playfield centre
label.availability: training loss and scoring only; never an input, never a history field, never a pixel region, never a tensor of the policy head
label.player_x_source: the frozen round19 teacher_v2 action list replayed through the unmodified `advance` (train), or the checkpoint's own stored x_before (scoring); both are the visible state

supervision.window: the rows whose logical frame 2*i lies inside round21.telegraph_window(s) = [wall_frame-45, wall_frame)
supervision.rule_text: the sign is taken at the FIRST decision row whose logical frame lies inside round21.telegraph_window(s) = [wall_frame-45, wall_frame) and applied to every supervised row of that event; per-row signs, flip rows and flip frames are recorded for every event and reported, and the per-row variant is not tried
supervision.why: outside the telegraph window the band is not drawn yet, so the label would ask the head to guess rather than to read; F2/F3 worlds have `internal_gap = False` and therefore no label at all
supervision.flips: per-row signs, flip rows and flip frames are recorded for every event and reported (labels.json, probes.json); the per-row variant is NOT tried in this round
supervision.labelled_events: the six F1 train events (3 groups x base/mirror)
supervision.unlabelled_events: the eight F2/F3 train events contribute an exactly-zero auxiliary term

intervention.loss: L = L_control + w * CE(aux_logits, side);  w = 0.0 for arm A, 0.5 for arm X
intervention.gradient_path: the auxiliary term reaches only the auxiliary head and the shared GRU
intervention.head_class: round23's PrivAuxPolicy, reused: no line of TacticalPolicy is overridden
intervention.not_changed: worlds, world parameters, R19 split, round21 renderer and pixels, teacher actions, tactical labels, pixel packing, encoder, control loss, optimizer, learning rate, clip value, clip scope, sequence, batch, update count, seed set, closed-loop runner, condition, masking, head, weight, supervision window
intervention.parameter_increment: X and A are identical objects: 429200 policy-head parameters + 514 auxiliary parameters = 429714 active; the arms differ only in w

data.source: round21 run/records.json assets, reopened read-only and SHA-bound per event; nothing re-rendered, no teacher executed, no tactical label created
data.features: round22.spatial_vectors reused verbatim; its spatial digest must recompute to round22's frozen 83a75f73... so "the head sees round22's features" is a measured identity, not a copy
data.teacher: round19 run/worlds/<family>/<event>.json teacher_v2 action lists; for the 14 train events they are asserted equal to round21's stored rollout actions

train.use: the only events encoded or trained on

validation.use: read-only: never trained, never encoded into the training set; closed loop and probes only. The auxiliary probe reads the label at that checkpoint's own first preview row and uses it only to score

data.bindings: pixels.npz, history.pt, labels.pt and rollout.json must equal round21's frozen SHA table for all 14 train events, otherwise the run aborts

arms.A: the same auxiliary head with weight 0.0: the round23 control
arms.X: the same auxiliary head with weight 0.5

training.clip_scope: the 429200 policy-head parameters, identically in both arms
training.precision: FP32 without AMP, autocast disabled, matmul TF32 False, cuDNN TF32 False, float32 matmul precision highest
training.loop: round23.train_all with one change: the target/mask pair per event comes from sign(gap centre - player x) instead of gap centre > 192
training.initialization: fresh seed reset per construction; the head is built first, so the policy head SHA must equal the frozen R16/R20/R21/R22/R23 table for the seed; the auxiliary head is built afterwards from the same RNG state in both arms, so its SHA must be identical in both arms
training.control_reproduction: arm A must reproduce round23's A checkpoint SHA and every closed-loop row bitwise; if it does not, that is reported as `control_not_reproduced` and the causal claim is withheld
training.selection: final step only: no early stopping, no validation-based selection, no tuning; the auxiliary weight is fixed at 0.5 before the run

evaluation.order: all six checkpoints written and SHA-frozen first; then the six R18 baselines, then B0, then the six checkpoints, validation before train; then the probes
evaluation.executor: round21.closed_loop reused verbatim through round23, so the evaluation code is round21 code and not a copy; the network is a plain TacticalPolicy
evaluation.b0: the frozen baseline policy logits on the identical telegraph renders
evaluation.six_baselines: round20.six_baselines re-executed on the same worlds; the 168 rows must equal round22's
evaluation.holdout_rule: if ANY of the six R18 baselines is feasible on ANY validation event the R18 filter has failed on the holdout side: report it verbatim and withhold the learning conclusion

definitions.toward: the canonical direction points from the start at the gap's canonical centre
definitions.parked: `signed_error_px` at wall_frame-1 in canonical px: 0 inside [gap0, gap1]
definitions.label: sign(gap screen centre - player screen x) at the first preview row, where player x is `render_state`'s own x and `advance` moves it by 2*action
definitions.agreement: the label against the teacher's own first action (episode decision 0) and against the teacher's action at the anchoring row; a hold action is counted separately and excluded from the rate
definitions.aux_accuracy: the auxiliary head on the preview-window rows of the six F1 validation events, replayed along each checkpoint's own stored trajectory

primary_metrics: K1: F1 holdout feasible per seed, X minus A
K2: pooled feasible over the three seeds, F1 and all-family
K3: mirror-group toward rate (and base), per arm, with the per-seed split
K4: cells inside the gap at wall_frame-1 and the signed parking error in px
K5: the auxiliary head's held-out accuracy, balanced accuracy and 2x2 confusion
the label diagnostics: the per-row sign/flip table, the label-vs-teacher agreement on both splits, and the count of mirror cells where the head read right and the policy went the other way

probe_caveats.aux_accuracy: the frozen teacher labels are balanced 3/3 on both splits, so chance is 0.5; a checkpoint whose own trajectory flips the sign moves its cell label, and that is reported per cell rather than hidden
probe_caveats.label_leakage: both the gap and the player are visible in the telegraph window, so the auxiliary task adds no information that is not in the pixels - it adds a target. What is privileged is the label, not the content
probe_caveats.decodability: 132 rows against 256 dimensions with a label constant within an event: only the whole lambda sweep and the arm-to-arm comparison are read
probe_caveats.replay: the replay re-renders each checkpoint's own x trace; its fidelity is reported for every cell

evaluation.reporting: per family, never only aggregated; n=3 seeds; F2 validation has one group; mirrors are not independent samples; every F1 cell is listed
evaluation.degeneracy: single_candidate and switches<=1 are counted, listed and reported

judgement.K1: F1 holdout feasible is strictly higher on at least two of the three seeds AND lower on none
judgement.K2: the pooled feasible counts over the three seeds: F1 and all-family; improved requires neither to fall
judgement.K3: mirror-group toward rate, reported as counts and rates, never as significance
judgement.K4: cells inside the gap at the wall and the signed parking error in px
judgement.K5: the auxiliary head's held-out balanced accuracy per seed; "learned" requires all three seeds above 0.5
judgement.rule: X is improved over A iff K1 holds and K2 does not fall; K1 with a falling pooled count is `mixed` and the word improved is not used; K1 false is one of `unchanged` (all equal), `not_improved` (both a rise and a fall), `worse` (no rise) or `inconclusive` (exactly one rise, no fall)
judgement.replaces: round23's rule "any seed strictly greater = improved", which scored -1/+1/0 as improved while the pooled total fell from 9 to 6
judgement.mixed: if K1 holds but K2 falls the round reports `mixed`; mechanism counters are reported next to it so the two are never read apart
judgement.honesty: if the mirror direction does not improve while the auxiliary head is accurate, the round must report the "the task was learned, the policy did not use it" reading with its cell-level evidence and compare its mirror cell count with round23's 8/9; if the label's agreement with the teacher is low, the report must state that this label cannot be the ground truth for "which way to move" and bound the conclusion
judgement.aux_learned: the auxiliary task counts as learned on the holdout only if the balanced accuracy exceeds 0.5 for all three seeds; a single seed above chance is reported as one seed, not as learned

claims.significance: none: 3 seeds, 7 validation groups, at most 14 independent geometries; descriptive only
claims.gate: no formal gate opened, no deployable checkpoint produced, no game executed
claims.can_show: whether replacing a position-fact label with the action-sign label changes the F1 holdout direction structure, and whether the residual failure is the label definition or the coupling between the GRU state and the policy head
claims.cannot_show: tactical understanding, learnability beyond these 7 held-out geometries, or that a privileged label at training time is a legitimate route to a deployable policy

criterion.failure_policy: first failure retained; one run; no retrain, rerun, repair of numbers, extra epoch, tuning or baseline switch

split.rule: one group = base + mirror, atomic; within each family the groups are ordered by group name (candidate index) and alternate train/validation starting with train at index 0; the two F2 groups therefore give one train and one validation group

auxiliary.task: from the GRU state predict whether the safe gap lies left or right OF THE PLAYER, i.e. which sign of action closes the distance to the slot: label = sign(gap screen centre - player screen x), gap from round21.telegraph_gap(s) (privileged world parameter), player x from the frozen teacher trajectory (train) or the checkpoint's own trajectory (scoring); the label is read at the first row of the telegraph window
auxiliary.label_rule_text: the sign is taken at the FIRST decision row whose logical frame lies inside round21.telegraph_window(s) = [wall_frame-45, wall_frame) and applied to every supervised row of that event; per-row signs, flip rows and flip frames are recorded for every event and reported, and the per-row variant is not tried
auxiliary.supervision_window: the rows whose logical frame 2*i lies inside round21.telegraph_window(s) = [wall_frame-45, wall_frame)
auxiliary.head: Linear(256, 2, bias=True) outside `heads` (round23's class, reused)
auxiliary.parent_detach: inert: the auxiliary head is downstream of the GRU
auxiliary.inference: the closed loop builds a plain TacticalPolicy from payload["heads"]; the auxiliary state is never loaded and there is no module to hold it

labels.rule_text: the sign is taken at the FIRST decision row whose logical frame lies inside round21.telegraph_window(s) = [wall_frame-45, wall_frame) and applied to every supervised row of that event; per-row signs, flip rows and flip frames are recorded for every event and reported, and the per-row variant is not tried

labels.note: the teacher trajectory is used here; a checkpoint's own trajectory is scored with the same rule and its flips are reported in probes.json

agreement.note: the label never predicts hold, so a hold first action is counted separately and excluded from the rate; F2/F3 worlds have no gap and therefore no label

round23_collinearity.note: `round23_side` is round23's label (gap centre above 192); `player_screen_half` is the player's own visible x above 192 at the same row. Where the two coincide, round23's target was a statement about the player, not about the gap

features.note: the 94-d spatial vector that function also returns is not used; it is the frozen proof that the encode pass is round22's

initialization.method: fresh seed reset immediately before every N1 construction after the backbone load, through the frozen r16 recipe; the auxiliary head is constructed afterwards, so it cannot move the head initialisation and both arms are byte-identical objects at step 0

round23_reference.label: round23 label = gap screen centre above x=192 (the playfield centre), not above the player

comparison.note: round23's rule was "any seed larger = improved"; this round replaces it with K1 and the mixed verdict

round23_reference.behaviour: round23: screen directions 12R/3L/3hold (A) -> 17R/1L/0hold (X); mirror toward rate 3/9 -> 1/9; the auxiliary head read the mirror side correctly in 8/9 cells while the policy moved away in 8/9

prerequisites: every training asset equals round21's frozen SHA
the round22 spatial digest recomputes to 83a75f73...
the round22 feature-norm table recomputes exactly
the round19 teacher_v2 table equals round21's stored rollout actions
the initial head SHA equals the frozen table for every seed
the six R18 baselines reproduce round22's 168 rows
verification.control: arm A must equal round23's A checkpoint SHA and its closed-loop rows for all 3 seeds; otherwise it is reported as `control_not_reproduced` and the causal claim is withheld
verification.step0: a unit test asserts that step 0 of arm X is bitwise arm A and that perturbing the auxiliary parameters changes no policy logit

failure_policy: first failure retained; one run; no retrain, rerun, repair or overwrite
